enriched_description: Handheld power tool for drilling holes, consisting of a pistol-grip body housing an electric motor (corded or battery-powered) with a rotating chuck at the front. Chuck is a three-jaw mechanism (keyed or keyless) that grips drill bits of various diameters. Body is constructed from molded plastic and metal, typically 20-30 cm in length. Trigger switch on the grip controls speed, with a forward/reverse selector above the trigger. Battery variants feature a detachable battery pack at the base of the grip. Surface exhibits textured grip panels, ventilation slots, and brand labeling. Distinguishing features include rotating chuck assembly, pistol-grip ergonomics, and variable-speed trigger control.

Small rectangular woven rug used for Islamic devotions, typically 70 x 120 cm in size. Surface features a woven pile or flat-weave construction with a distinctive mihrab (arch) design at one end, indicating the direction of prayer (qibla). Pattern includes geometric, floral, or calligraphic motifs in rich colors (red, blue, green, gold, ivory). Fringed edges at both ends are characteristic. Material is wool, cotton, or synthetic fiber with a soft, textured surface. Central field may contain medallion or repeating border patterns. Distinguishing features include arch-shaped mihrab motif, fringed termini, and portable devotional rug proportions.

Computer peripheral output device that produces hardcopy documents on paper. Desktop variants are rectangular box-shaped units (40-50 cm wide, 30-40 cm deep, 15-25 cm tall) constructed from white, gray, or black plastic. Front features a paper output tray, control panel with LCD display and buttons, and status indicator LEDs. Paper input tray is located at rear or bottom. Inkjet variants have visible ink cartridge access doors; laser variants have a toner cartridge compartment. Top surface may include a flatbed scanner lid (multifunction models). Distinguishing features include paper input/output trays, compact desktop footprint, and document-output function.

Secure correctional facility characterized by high perimeter walls topped with barbed wire or razor wire, guard towers at corners, and reinforced entry gates. Building construction uses brick, concrete, or stone with small barred or reinforced windows. Exterior exhibits a utilitarian, imposing architectural style with minimal decorative elements. Watchtowers feature elevated platforms with 360-degree visibility. Fencing includes chain-link or steel palisade with anti-climb features. Overall scale is large, covering multiple acres with cell blocks, administrative buildings, and recreational yards. Distinguishing features include perimeter security walls, guard towers, barred windows, and fortified entry points.

Non-self-propelled weapon designed to be thrown, launched, or fired at a target. Forms include spherical (cannonball, musket ball), cylindrical (arrow, bolt, spear), or aerodynamic (javelin, dart) geometries. Materials range from stone and metal to composite constructions. Surface exhibits smooth, polished, or machined finishes depending on manufacturing method. Aerodynamic variants feature pointed tips, stabilizing fins, or fletching. Dimensions vary from centimeters (bullets) to meters (siege projectiles). Distinguishing features include ballistic shape optimization, impact-oriented construction, and launch-compatible geometry.

Optical instrument that projects enlarged images onto a screen or surface. Box-shaped housing (30-50 cm wide, 25-40 cm deep, 10-20 cm tall) constructed from plastic or metal with ventilation grilles. Front features a prominent projection lens assembly with focus and zoom rings. Top or rear includes input ports (HDMI, VGA, USB) and control buttons. Lens is centered on the front face, surrounded by a recessed bezel. Cooling fans produce audible operation noise. Ceiling-mount variants include mounting brackets. Distinguishing features include front-facing projection lens, ventilation grille pattern, and rectangular optical-housing form factor.

Solid vulcanized rubber disk used in ice hockey, exactly 2.54 cm (1 inch) thick and 7.62 cm (3 inches) in diameter, weighing 156-170 grams. Surface is matte black with a smooth, slightly textured finish. Edge features raised ridges or grooves (typically 4-6) around the circumference to improve stick handling and reduce bouncing. Faces may bear printed league logos, brand markings, or game identification numbers. Material is dense and hard, producing a characteristic sharp sound when struck. Distinguishing features include precise 3-inch diameter disk geometry, circumferential edge ridges, and matte black vulcanized rubber appearance.

Cylindrical or teardrop-shaped training bag suspended from a ceiling mount or stand, filled with fabric, sand, or foam for impact absorption. Heavy bags are 90-150 cm tall and 30-45 cm in diameter, constructed from leather, vinyl, or canvas with a smooth or slightly textured surface. Color is typically black, red, or brown. Top features reinforced hanging loops or chains connecting to a swivel mount. Surface shows wear patterns from repeated strikes. Speed bags are smaller, tear-shaped, and mounted on a rebound platform. Distinguishing features include elongated cylindrical form, suspended hanging configuration, and impact-resistant outer material.

Small handheld bag for carrying personal items and money, typically 15-30 cm in width and 10-20 cm in height. Constructed from leather, fabric, or synthetic materials with a zippered, snap, or flap closure. Surface may be smooth, textured, embossed, or decorated with hardware (buckles, chains, logos). Interior contains compartments, card slots, and a coin pocket. Strap may be a short handle, detachable shoulder strap, or chain. Color ranges from neutral (black, brown, tan) to vibrant hues. Distinguishing features include compact handheld scale, secure closure mechanism, and personal-carry accessory design.

Writing implement crafted from a large bird's flight feather (typically goose, swan, or turkey), 20-40 cm in total length. The feather shaft (calamus) is hollow and translucent, with a naturally curved form. The distal end is cut to a sharp nib point, often split to create an ink channel. Barbs extend laterally from the shaft, creating the characteristic feathery appearance. Color ranges from white to gray, brown, or black depending on the bird species. The nib end may show ink staining from use. Distinguishing features include natural feather morphology, hollow shaft construction, and hand-cut nib tip.
